text.p: Federal-Mogul Co, a manufacturer of parts for cars, trucks and farm vehicles, said North American replacement business posted essentially flat third-quarter sales compared to $191 million in 1995.
It said consolidation of businesses within the replacement channel, reduction in inventories at the customer level and mild weather contributed to the softness.
Internationally, it said the replacement business in the quarter accounted for a six percent sales increase to $149 million from $140 million.
Sales were hurt by foreign exchange, primarily in South America and Venezuela, but offset by the 1995 acquisition of Centropiezas in Puerto Rico.
Earlier Friday, Federal-Mogul reported a third-quarter loss of $0.56 per share, which included a $0.70 per share charge. Sales advanced to $491.6 million from $480.2 million.
It said its North American original equipment business posted a 14 percent rise in sales to $111 million from $98 million, while internationally this segment's sales were essentially flat.
